source: In return, Eliza sings only one word: helpless. It is the last time she sings
why: The data has no lyric text or word-level column; characters.csv records only line ranges and characters.csv/themes.csv do not identify the word 'helpless' or the last song in which it is sung.

source: The songs are filtered by two recurring phrases of Contentment: "that would be enough" and "look around at how lucky we are to be alive right now".
why: themes.csv stores numeric theme IDs, notes, line ranges and songs, but no phrase text, so the two named phrases cannot be tied to theme IDs or songs from the files.

source: Many of the themes are blank
why: The story gives no definition or count for 'blank', and themes.csv cannot distinguish an intentionally blank theme from an unlabelled one, so no checkable number or pattern follows.

source: Some characters, conversations, or themes will disappear as you filter down; their co-appearances and co-occurrences are often times just as interesting as the songs that are left.
why: This describes interactive filtering behavior without a specific number, comparison, ranking, share, trend or named pattern to test against the data.
